_comment: Windows logging a CONSUMER must have before a hunt hypothesis can be tested — telemetry need -> audit setting. Keys under `settings` are the valid telemetry_priorities[].baseline_ref values (report_sections.py lint; report_sections.json actor_profile.pointers.telemetry_baselines_index). Written in our own words from Yamato Security's EventLog-Baseline-Guide (MIT; attribution below). No rule, hunt or script text is copied. The guide supplies the subcategories, each baseline's recommended setting, the per-setting rule counts, the usable/unusable rule totals and the log sizes. The event IDs are standard Microsoft event IDs that we list for orientation; they are not taken from the guide. cti-expert never applies these settings and never reads a consumer's logs: the consumer checks its own estate.

source._comment: Provenance of everything below: the guide, the commit every link is pinned to, and the MIT attribution this adaptation must carry.
source.name: EventLog-Baseline-Guide
source.attribution: Adapted from Yamato Security's EventLog-Baseline-Guide, Copyright (c) 2025 YamatoSecurity, MIT License.

sources._comment: Pinned files the numbers below are read from. *_audit = WELA-Audit-Result.csv (per-setting default, recommended setting, rule count, volume note); *_usable / *_unusable = the rule lists counted for `baselines`; *_sizes = WELA-FileSize-Result.csv; *_bat = the baseline's configuration script.

baselines._comment: The configurations the guide compares, scored by how many of the same 2,553 Hayabusa-format Sigma rules could fire under each (usable) or could not (unusable). Numbers are rows counted in the guide's own UsableRules.csv / UnusableRules.csv at the pinned commit — the guide's measurement, not ours. A rule being usable means its log source is on; it says nothing about whether the rule is tuned.

windows_default.label: Windows out of the box (the comparison floor)
windows_default.covers: Only what Windows logs unconfigured: no process creation, no PowerShell module logging, partial script-block logging, 20 MB Security log.

yamato_security.label: Yamato Security recommended
yamato_security.covers: Broadest Security-log subcategory set (incl. Filtering Platform Connection, Security System Extension, Sensitive Privilege Use), PowerShell module + script-block logging, Task Scheduler Operational enabled, command line in 4688, large logs.

microsoft_client.label: Microsoft recommendation, client
microsoft_client.covers: Core logon, account and process-creation (success only) auditing with command line; no PowerShell logging and no log-size change.

microsoft_server.label: Microsoft recommendation, server
microsoft_server.covers: As the client baseline plus account/group-management failures and Security System Extension; no PowerShell logging and no log-size change.

asd.label: Australian Signals Directorate (ASD)
asd.covers: Logon, account, process-creation (success only, with command line) and object auditing, PowerShell module + script-block logging, a 2 GB Security log. Highest usable count in the guide's data.

settings._comment: One entry per telemetry need. category/subcategory: the guide's names (Security Advanced = Advanced Audit Policy). default: Windows' own state. recommended: each baseline's setting per its WELA-Audit-Result.csv ("" = that baseline makes no recommendation). sigma_rules: the guide's rule count depending on this setting. event_ids: ours, for orientation (standard Microsoft IDs). volume: the guide's volume note, paraphrased.

process_creation_cmdline.name: Audit Process Creation + include command line
process_creation_cmdline.also: Policy 'Include command line in process creation events' (ProcessCreationIncludeCmdLine_Enabled); every baseline script sets it.
process_creation_cmdline.enables: Every new process with its parent and full command line — the source most behavioural hunts need when Sysmon is absent.
process_creation_cmdline.volume: High; the guide treats it as needed when Sysmon is not deployed.

logon.name: Audit Logon
logon.enables: Successful and failed logons with logon type and source address — lateral movement, brute force, RDP use.
logon.default: Client OS: Success | Server OS: Success and Failure
logon.volume: Low on clients, medium on domain controllers and network servers.

special_logon.name: Audit Special Logon
special_logon.volume: Low on clients, medium on domain controllers and network servers.

credential_validation.name: Audit Credential Validation
credential_validation.enables: NTLM credential checks — password spraying and NTLM relay traces.
credential_validation.default: Client OS: No Auditing | Server OS: Success
credential_validation.volume: Depends on NTLM use; can be high on domain controllers.

kerberos_authentication.name: Audit Kerberos Authentication Service (domain controllers)
kerberos_authentication.enables: TGT requests and pre-authentication failures — AS-REP roasting and password guessing against the domain.
kerberos_authentication.default: Client OS: No Auditing | Server OS: Success

recommended.yamato_security: Server OS: Success and Failure (clients: No Auditing)

account_lockout.name: Audit Account Lockout
account_lockout.enables: Logon failures caused by a locked account — brute-force signal.

user_account_management.name: Audit User Account Management
user_account_management.enables: Account creation, enablement, password resets and changes — persistence through new or revived accounts.

security_group_management.name: Audit Security Group Management
security_group_management.enables: Members added to security groups — privilege escalation into admin groups.

scheduled_task_audit.name: Audit Other Object Access Events
scheduled_task_audit.enables: Scheduled tasks created, deleted or changed — a common persistence and execution path.

task_scheduler_operational.name: Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational log enabled
task_scheduler_operational.enables: The task scheduler's own record of task registration and runs; complements 4698.

service_install.name: Audit Security System Extension
service_install.enables: Services installed on the host (Security-log view; the System log's 7045 is on by default).

registry_sacl.name: Audit Registry (with targeted SACLs)
registry_sacl.enables: Changes to registry keys that carry an audit SACL — Run keys and other autoruns, if the consumer sets SACLs on them.
registry_sacl.volume: Depends on the SACLs; the guide advises SACLs only on the keys you want to watch.

network_connection_wfp.name: Audit Filtering Platform Connection
network_connection_wfp.enables: Per-process network connections allowed or blocked — beaconing and lateral movement without Sysmon.
network_connection_wfp.volume: High; the guide suggests it only with enough log space and when Sysmon does not already log network connections.

powershell_script_block.name: PowerShell Script Block Logging
powershell_script_block.enables: The de-obfuscated script text PowerShell actually ran.
powershell_script_block.default: Partially Enabled (only scripts AMSI flags as suspicious, Windows 10/Server 2016 on)

powershell_module.name: PowerShell Module Logging
powershell_module.enables: Pipeline execution detail per command, including parameters.

defender_operational.name: Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender/Operational
defender_operational.enables: Detections, remediation and protection being switched off.

system_log.name: System log
system_log.enables: Service installs and state changes, log clearing of other channels.

wmi_activity.name: Microsoft-Windows-WMI-Activity/Operational
wmi_activity.enables: WMI providers and permanent event subscriptions — WMI persistence.

sysmon_optional.name: Sysmon (optional add-on, not a built-in audit setting)
sysmon_optional.enables: Richer process, network, image-load, file, registry and DNS events than the built-in audit policy, if the consumer deploys it.

recommended.yamato_security: Optional; if used, size its log to 1 GB

sysmon_optional.volume: Configuration-dependent; the guide does not score Sysmon rules.

log_sizes._comment: The guide's log-size guidance. `recommended_floor` is the guide's Recommended column; the baseline columns are the maximum size each baseline sets (Windows default when the baseline leaves it alone). Small logs roll over within hours on a busy host, so a hunt window longer than the retained history cannot be tested.
